paper_cards.title: Conditional neural field latent diffusion model for generating spatiotemporal turbulence

key_results.text: CoNFiLD enables memory-efficient and robust generation of turbulence under diverse conditions by integrating conditional neural field encoding with latent diffusion processes. [Abstract]
CoNFiLD supports applications such as zero-shot full-field flow reconstruction from sparse sensor data, super-resolution generation, and spatiotemporal data restoration. [Abstract]
Extensive numerical experiments demonstrate CoNFiLD's capability to accurately generate inhomogeneous, anisotropic turbulent flows within complex domains. [Abstract]
CoNFiLD has the potential to serve as a versatile, computationally efficient tool for real-time unsteady turbulence simulation, advancing digital twin technology for fluid dynamics. [Abstract]

method.text: The CoNFiLD model integrates conditional neural field encoding with latent diffusion processes to enable efficient high-fidelity stochastic generation of spatiotemporal turbulent flows in complex, three-dimensional domains. [Abstract]
CoNFiLD leverages Bayesian conditional sampling to flexibly adapt to various turbulence generation scenarios without retraining. [Abstract]

setup.text: The paper focuses on generating inhomogeneous, anisotropic turbulent flows within complex, three-dimensional domains. [Abstract]

limitations.text: Traditional numerical methods like DNS and LES face severe computational limitations, restricting their use in high-Reynolds number or real-time scenarios. [Abstract]

Recent deep learning-based surrogate models often rely on deterministic frameworks, which struggle to capture the chaotic and stochastic nature of turbulence, especially under varying physical conditions and complex, irregular geometries. [Abstract]

paper_cards.title: A Latent Space Framework for Modeling Transient Engine Emissions Using Joint Embedding Predictive Architectures
paper_cards.venue: SAE technical papers on CD-ROM/SAE technical paper series

key_results.text: The proposed JEPA framework demonstrates superior data efficiency and predictive accuracy across diverse transient regimes compared to LSTM baselines. [P1]
Structured pruning and post-training quantization significantly reduce the model’s computational footprint (inference time and memory demand) with only marginal impact on accuracy. [P1]
The latent space abstraction enables robust encoding of key emission dynamics while filtering out irrelevant information, improving generalization under dataset variability. [P1]

method.text: A Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) is used to model transient engine emissions in a structured latent space. [P1]
The JEPA learns to abstract away irrelevant information and encode only the key factors governing emission behavior into a compact, robust latent representation. [P1]
The framework combines real-world driving data from a Portable Emission Measurement System (PEMS) with high-frequency hardware-in-the-loop test bench measurements for training. [P1]
Post-training quantization and structured pruning are applied to optimize the model for on-board deployment in conventional and hybrid electric powertrains. [P1]

setup.text: Training data integrates PEMS real-world driving records with high-frequency hardware-in-the-loop test bench measurements. [P1]
Baseline comparison includes Multilayer Perceptrons (MLPs) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks as conventional data-driven models. [P1]
Evaluation focuses on transient emission prediction accuracy, data efficiency, and computational footprint for embedded deployment. [P1]

limitations.text: Conventional monolithic architectures (e.g., MLPs, LSTMs) struggle to capture complex nonlinear emission dynamics and are sensitive to dataset variability. [P1]
Increasing architectural depth/complexity in traditional models limits practical utility despite marginal performance gains. [P1]
The JEPA approach requires careful tuning of latent space dimensionality and prediction objectives to balance abstraction fidelity and predictive power. [P1]

paper_cards.title: Hybrid Server–AI Architecture for Persistent Generative Game Worlds: Achieving Scalable, Consistent, and Low-Latency Interactive Environments
paper_cards.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

key_results.text: The proposed hybrid server–AI architecture achieves scalable, consistent, and low-latency interactive environments by fusing deterministic server frameworks with state-aware generative systems. [Abstract]

The three-tier design includes a deterministic server backend, a state-aware generative layer, and an AI-driven post-processing enhancement system that reduces computational overhead by 60–80% relative to full generative rendering while maintaining high visual fidelity. [Abstract]

Novel synchronization mechanisms, including a content-addressable generation ledger and a generative determinism envelope, ensure causal coherence, fairness, and identity continuity across sessions. [Abstract]

Performance modeling indicates the system can sustain thousands of concurrent users with sub-100 ms end-to-end latency, supported by predictive asset prefetching, hierarchical level-of-detail strategies, and progressive enhancement pipelines. [Abstract]

The framework provides a practical and scalable pathway for deploying persistent generative game worlds, bridging a critical gap between cutting-edge AI content generation and the proven stability of modern multiplayer infrastructures. [Abstract]

The approach has direct applicability to both entertainment and serious games, enabling new genres that combine emergent creativity with persistent, socially complex, and economically rich virtual environments. [Abstract]

method.text: The deterministic server backend leverages technologies such as Unity Netcode for GameObjects, Unreal Engine 5’s dedicated servers, and Amazon GameLift to maintain authoritative and persistent world state. [Abstract]
The state-aware generative layer is responsible for producing real-time environmental, character, and interactive assets informed by canonical game state. [Abstract]
The AI-driven post-processing enhancement system applies neural rendering, upscaling, and detail synthesis to lightweight base scenes. [Abstract]
The architecture introduces a content-addressable generation ledger and a generative determinism envelope to ensure causal coherence, fairness, and identity continuity across sessions. [Abstract]
Predictive asset prefetching, hierarchical level-of-detail strategies, and progressive enhancement pipelines are used to support sub-100 ms end-to-end latency. [Abstract]

setup.text: The deterministic server backend utilizes Unity Netcode for GameObjects, Unreal Engine 5’s dedicated servers, and Amazon GameLift. [Abstract]

paper_cards.title: A Latent Space Framework for Modeling Transient Engine Emissions Using Joint Embedding Predictive Architectures

key_results.text: The proposed JEPA-based framework achieves superior data efficiency and predictive accuracy across diverse transient regimes compared to high-performing LSTM baselines in generalization. [page P]
The model successfully abstracts away irrelevant noise, encoding only the key factors governing emission behavior into a compact, robust representation. [page P]
The JEPA framework supports pruning and post-training quantization, drastically reducing computational footprint while maintaining negligible accuracy loss. [page P]

The resulting model is highly efficient for on-board implementation of advanced control strategies such as model predictive control or model-based reinforcement learning in conventional and hybrid powertrains. [page P]

method.text: A novel latent space framework is introduced using a Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) to model transient engine emissions. [page P]
The JEPA learns from a combined dataset of real-world Portable Emission Measurement System (PEMS) data and high-frequency hardware-in-the-loop measurements. [page P]
The architecture encodes emission dynamics into a structured latent representation that captures key behavioral factors while filtering out noise. [page P]
The framework is designed to be compatible with model compression techniques including pruning and post-training quantization for deployment efficiency. [page P]

setup.text: The model is trained on a rich dataset combining real-world PEMS data with high-frequency hardware-in-the-loop measurements. [page P]
Performance is evaluated against monolithic architectures including Multilayer Perceptrons (MLPs) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks. [page P]
Evaluation focuses on generalization performance across diverse transient driving regimes. [page P]
Deployment suitability is assessed through computational footprint analysis after applying pruning and quantization. [page P]

limitations.text: Conventional data-driven methods like MLPs and LSTMs struggle with complex nonlinear dynamics of emission formation and are sensitive to dataset variability. [page P]
Monolithic architectures typically require deep, computationally expensive structures to perform well, limiting practical utility. [page P]

The paper does not explicitly state limitations of the proposed JEPA framework itself, though it implies challenges related to training complexity and interpretability of latent representations may exist. [page P]
